articles.title: Interior Secretary’s Calendars Dominated by Big Oil and Big Tech, Analysis Finds
articles.description: During his first year as head of the U.S. Department of the Interior, Doug Burgum opened his door to a steady stream of corporate executives, trade associations, or their lobbyists, and an outsized proportion of those visitors were representatives of Big Oil and Big Tech, according to a new report released today by Public Citizen. Public Citizen’s analysis of Burgum’s publicly disclosed calendars identified 488 external visitors listed on Burgum’s public schedule and found that more than half, or 262, were corporate executives, trade associations, or their lobbyists. In contrast, Burgum met with 69 visitors from conservation, hunting, fishing, and other nonprofits, accounting for 14% of his visitors, and just 15 visitors from Native tribes. He also had 19 visitors from foreign governments in 2025. “Secretary Burgum’s schedule paints a picture of an official who shows little care for the core mission of the Department of the Interior, while his office becomes a key influence-peddling stop for energy, technology, and finance executives,” said Alan Zibel, a research director with Public Citizen and author of the report. “Burgum’s calendar contains frequent panel discussions, dinners and speaking events with titans of tech, energy and finance but scant focus on our public lands, which have faced mounting attacks.” The Interior Department did not disclose the calendars voluntarily, releasing the 2025 calendars to the public only after a lawsuit by the Sierra Club. The department has not disclosed his calendars for 2026 so far. The analysis of Burgum’s 2025 calendars reveals a clear pattern of promoting corporate interests while deviating from the Interior Department’s core functions, trading the management of national parks and oversight of federal responsibilities to Native American tribes for a flashier profile leading Trump’s National Energy Dominance Council. During his tenure at the Department of the Interior, Burgum has used his time to push the global expansion of oil and gas production, making him a central figure in Trump’s foreign policy misadventures in Iran and Venezuela. His actions promoting Trump’s dangerous energy agenda include citing “national security” to exempt Gulf of Mexico oil and gas drilling from the Endangered Species Act and pushing for offshore drilling off the coast of California, including the use of special wartime authority to force the restart of drilling on a platform that had been idle since 2015 following a disastrous oil spill. Technology has little to do with the Interior Department’s mission, but Burgum has harnessed and bolstered business contacts he made during his former career as a technology executive. Corporate visitors included executives from the largest Big Tech companies, many of which are making huge data center investments, including executives from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta, Oracle and SpaceX, as well as financial industry titans from Blackstone, Citadel and many others. Additionally, top officials from the United Arab Emirates — Ambassador Yousef Al Otaiba and Sultan Al Jaber, UAE Minister of Industry and Advanced Technology and CEO of the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company — have entries on Burgum’s calendar, as do officials from Canada, Italy and Greece. “As Interior Secretary, Burgum has aggressively worked to redefine the job into a high-profile orchestrator of industry and government,” Zibel said. “But Burgum’s role cheerleading the agenda of America’s CEOs has come at the cost of protecting our public lands, our responsibilities to Native tribes, and investing in low-cost renewable energy. His calendars clearly illustrate how his distracted approach undermines the Interior Department’s goals.” Read the full report here.

articles.title: Thanksgiving Prices Jump 11% Under Trump, Gobbling Up More of Families’ Budgets
articles.description: Families will pay more for nearly everything on the Thanksgiving table this year, from the turkey to the fixings and holiday pies. A new analysis from Groundwork Collaborative and The Century Foundation finds that the cost of a traditional Thanksgiving dinner is up 11% over the past year, roughly three times the overall rate of inflation, making Thanksgiving yet another expensive holiday for families under President Trump. This year, frozen turkeys – once an affordable option for the Thanksgiving table’s centerpiece – will cost 26% more. Classic Thanksgiving sides will also take a bigger bite out of holiday grocery budgets. Fans of macaroni and cheese will face an astounding 40.2% price hike on elbow macaroni this year. Green bean casserole lovers are in for sticker shock, with green beans up 36.7% and cream of mushroom soup climbing 22.5%. Other holiday favorites have seen price hikes, too, including cornbread mix (9%) and candied yams (10.6%). Dessert offers no sweet relief this year: Pillsbury pie crust is up more than 6%, while Granny Smith apples and pecans have climbed 10%and 23%, respectively. Even wrapping up Thanksgiving leftovers will cost more, with Reynolds Wrap aluminum foil 22.3% more expensive. Higher prices for Thanksgiving staples this year trace back to Trump’s war with Iran and his erratic tariffs. While his war has sent fuel and fertilizer costs soaring, driving up the price of turkey and fresh produce, his tariffs have made traditionally affordable alternatives like canned goods more expensive this year. As prices continue to climb out of reach, recent polling finds that fewer Americans are planning to host Thanksgiving dinner than last year, and many plan to change menu items or cut back on guests. Nearly one-third find hosting this year a financial strain, while almost one in five expect to turn to buy now, pay later loans just to celebrate with loved ones. Groundwork Collaborative Senior Advisor for Economic Policy Emily DiVito shared her reaction: “Thanksiving dinner will cost families more this year thanks to Trump. His war with Iran and reckless tariffs are driving up the cost of nearly everything on the Thanksgiving table, from the turkey to the sides. Working families are in for an expensive holiday season, with less room in their budgets and little patience for a president who promised but failed to bring prices down.” Kyle Moore, Chief Economist at The Century Foundation, said: “Thanksgiving is supposed to be about gathering around the table, but this year many families are deciding how many people they can afford to feed. When the cost of a traditional dinner jumps 11% in a single year and nearly one in five Americans expect to rely on Buy Now, Pay Later loans just to celebrate, it’s a clear sign that household budgets are stretched to their limit. These price hikes are the result of policy choices, and families are footing the bill.”
